candidates.verdict: already production; recall gain real, fp still high

candidates.config: Qwen3 flags -> Qwen3 skeptic must name a failing input or drop
candidates.finding: the skeptic upholds the flagger's own FPs — confident hallucination survives self-interrogation; every surviving FP is on a live-mined case (real loop diffs), so this is exactly the production failure mode, not a corpus artifact. Also cost one true defect (recall 1.00->0.88).

design_conclusion: No fleet model, under any single-prompt or self-audit config tested, both catches defects and stays quiet on correct code (threshold recall>=0.75 AND fp<=0.25). The reviewer layer should therefore be ADVISORY (non-blocking) rather than gating until either (a) a cross-model skeptic is tried (different family auditing Qwen3's findings) or (b) a frontier reviewer is used for supervised runs (PXX_REVIEW_BACKEND=claude already exists). The deterministic gates + hidden eval checks remain the load-bearing independent layer regardless.
